questions.solution:

• **Computer Technology is based on Digital logic principles.**

 __

questions.question: Mac is a type of personal computer made by:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Apple**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Apple Inc.** is an American multinational technology company headquartered in Cupertino, California.
 
• Apple is known for its innovative technology products, including the Mac, iPhone, iPad, and Apple Watch.
 
• The first Macintosh computer, commonly known as Mac, was introduced by Apple in 1984.
 
• Apple's Mac computers are known for their sleek design, robust operating system (macOS), and high performance.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Personal Computer (PC)**

 
 
• A personal computer is a general-purpose computer designed for individual use.
 
• PCs are intended for use by one person at a time, and they are characterized by their size, capabilities, and relatively low cost.
 
• They are commonly used for tasks such as word processing, internet browsing, gaming, and multimedia playback.
 
• PCs can run a variety of operating systems, including Microsoft Windows, macOS, and Linux.
 
 
 
• **macOS**
 
 
• macOS is a series of proprietary graphical operating systems developed and marketed by Apple Inc. since 2001.
 
• It is the primary operating system for Apple's Mac family of computers.
 
• macOS is known for its intuitive user interface, stability, and security features.
 
• The latest version of macOS as of 2023 is macOS Ventura.
 
 
 
• **Apple Inc.**
 
 
• Apple Inc. was founded by Steve Jobs, Steve Wozniak, and Ronald Wayne in April 1976.
 
• Apple designs, manufactures, and markets a range of personal computers, mobile communication devices, and portable digital music players.
 
• Some of Apple's most popular products include the iPhone, iPad, Mac computers, Apple Watch, and Apple TV.
 
• Apple is also known for its software products, including the iOS operating system, iTunes media player, Safari web browser, and iWork suite of productivity software.
 
 
 
• **Innovations by Apple**
 
 
• Apple is credited with revolutionizing the personal computer industry with the introduction of the Macintosh in 1984.
 
• The iPhone, introduced in 2007, transformed the smartphone industry with its multi-touch interface and App Store.
 
• Apple's iPad, launched in 2010, created a new category of tablet computing devices.
 
• Apple continues to innovate with products like the Apple Watch, AirPods, and services like Apple Music and Apple TV+.

questions.question: Out of the 10 digits in the UPC barcode pattern, the first 5 digits identify the:

• The first Barcode system was developed by Norman Joseph Woodland.

 
 
• The barcode was invented by Norman Joseph Woodland and Bernard Silver and patented in the US in 1951.
 
• The invention was based on Morse code that was extended to thin and thick bars.
 
• Barcode contains information about a product like-

• A barcode scanner will read this pattern of black and white bars and translate them into a line of test that your retail point of sale system can understand.
 
• Barcodes are applied to products as a means of quick identification.
 
• They are used in retail stores as part of the purchase process, in warehouses to track inventory, and on invoices to assist in accounting, among many other uses.

questions.question: Which one of the following basic operations for converting raw input data into useful information is not performed by all computers?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Switching**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The basic operations for converting raw input data into useful information that are commonly performed by computers are **inputting, processing, storing, retrieving, and outputting**. 
 
• **Switching is not one of the basic operations for converting raw input data into useful information**__, as it is specific to computer networking and refers to the process of forwarding data packets between network nodes.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• Some basic operations for converting raw input data into useful information that are commonly performed by computers:

 
 
• **Input**: This involves the process of entering raw data into the computer system through various input devices like keyboards, scanners, or sensors.
 
• **Processing**: This refers to the manipulation of raw data by the computer system using various arithmetic and logical operations to produce meaningful output.
 
• **Storage**: This involves the retention of data in the computer's memory or storage devices like hard drives or cloud-based storage.
 
• **Retrieval**: This involves the process of accessing the stored data from the computer's memory or storage devices.
 
• **Output**: This involves the presentation of processed data or information to the user in a readable format through various output devices like monitors, printers, or speakers.

questions.question: Which of the following was Asia's first supercomputer?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**PARAM**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **PARAM** was developed by the Centre for Development of Advanced Computing (C-DAC) in India.
 
• It was launched in the year **1991** and marked India's entry into the field of supercomputing.
 
• PARAM is an acronym for **Parallel Machine**, reflecting its architecture and processing capabilities.
 
• It was a significant milestone in India's technological advancement and placed India among the few countries with supercomputing capabilities at that time.
 
• The development of PARAM was a response to the denial of supercomputing technology to India by other nations, showcasing India's self-reliance in high-performance computing.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• CRAY-3, although a notable supercomputer, was developed by the Cray Research company in the United States.
 
• EKA is another Indian supercomputer developed by the Computational Research Laboratories, but it was launched in **2007**.
 
• HITAC S-300 is a supercomputer developed by Hitachi, a Japanese company, and does not hold the distinction of being the first in Asia.
 
• PARAM's successful implementation led to the development of subsequent versions like PARAM 10000 and PARAM Yuva, further advancing India's supercomputing capabilities.

• Nowadays, generation includes both **hardware and software**, which together make up an entire computer system.

 Integrated Circuit based.

questions.question: ______ is the key circuit board holding the essential processing parts of a computer.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Motherboard**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Motherboard**: The motherboard is the main circuit board of a computer.

 
 
• It houses the **CPU, RAM, and other essential components.**
 
• It also provides the electrical connections by which the other components of the system communicate.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
 
 
 

 **Firmware**
 
 
Firmware is a type of software that provides control, monitoring and data manipulation of engineered products and systems.

 
It's typically stored in the read-only memory of a hardware device.

 
 
 

 **Central Processing Unit (CPU)**
 
 
The CPU is the primary component of a computer that performs most of the processing inside the computer.

 
It's often called the "brain" of the computer.

 
 
 

 **Random Access Memory (RAM)**
 
 
RAM is a type of computer memory that can be read from and written to by the processor.

 
It's a volatile memory, meaning it loses its contents when the computer is turned off or restarted.

questions.question: ______ is the process of turning on a computer and powering up the system.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Booting**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Booting is the process of turning on a computer and powering up the system**__. 

 __
 
• In other words, it is a startup sequence that starts the operating system of a computer when it is turned on.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **There are two types of Booting-**

 
 
• **Warm Booting**

 
 
• It is the process of restarting a computer.
 
• Warm boots are typically initiated by a "Restart" command in the operating system.
 
 
 
• **Cold Booting**
 
 
• It is the process of starting a computer from shutdown or a powerless state and setting it to normal working condition.
 
• It refers to the general process of starting the hardware components of a computer, laptop, or server to the point that its operating system and all startup applications and services are launched.
